docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
GVL Fix One is a high-accuracy RTK GNSS receiver for handheld or static applications.

  • Centimetre-level CEP real time, millimetre-level with postpocessing.

  • Dual-role Basestation and Rover

  • NTRIP transmit and receive

  • MQTT real time telemetry

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: GVL Fix One reads from a configuration file at startup to determine what to do.

docs.title: Accessing Storage
docs.text:
• Plug the the device into a computer

  • Hold power button to switch on

  • On boot screen, press any button.

  • A USB drive should show up on the computer

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
All files are stored at the root of the SD card.

  • Configuration File: gvl_config.txt
  • MQTT over TLS
    • Put the server CA certificate as mqtt.crt
    • Not needed for unencrypted MQTT

docs.title: Configuration Options
docs.text:
• Open gvl_config.txt with a text editor

Inside, there are multiple lines of option=value pairs.

Here's an example, details below.

nickname=gvl_test

wifi_ssid=myWifi
wifi_pass=hunter2

// 0: Rover, 1: Basestation
device_role=0

// 0: Wi-Fi, 1: Cellular, 2: No Comm.
comm_type=0

send_gga=1
use_mqtt=1

// Rover fix rate in Hz (1, 2, 5, or 10)
rover_refresh_rate=1

ntrip_addr=ntrip.data.gnss.ga.gov.au
ntrip_port=2101
ntrip_cred=username:password
ntrip_mountpoint=AUTO

mqtt_addr=test.mosquitto.org
mqtt_port=1883
mqtt_username=username
mqtt_password=password

  • Make sure there are no space before or after =

  • If an option is not present in the file, its value defaults to 0 or empty string

docs.title: device_role
docs.text:
Type Example Integer device_role=1

  • 0: Rover mode

  • 1: Basestation mode

docs.title: nickname
docs.text:
Type Example String nickname=gvl_test

  • Device nickname for easy identification

  • Included in MQTT message and logged files

docs.title: comm_type
docs.text:
Type Example Integer comm_type=1

  • 0: Use Wi-Fi for network connection

  • 1: Use Cellular for network connection

  • 2: No comms, won't connect to networks.

docs.title: wifi_ssid
docs.text:
Type Example String wifi_ssid=GVL_Demo
  • Name of the Wi-Fi Access Point

docs.title: wifi_pass
docs.text:
Type Example String wifi_ssid=hunter2
  • Password for the Wi-Fi Access Point

docs.title: ntrip_addr
docs.text:
Type Example String ntrip_addr=example.com

  • Address of the NTRIP server

  • Can be URL or IP address

docs.title: ntrip_port
docs.text:
Type Example Integer ntrip_port=2102
  • Port of the NTRIP server

docs.title: ntrip_cred
docs.text:
Type Example String ntrip_cred=username:password
  • Username and password for the NTRIP server, separated by : symbol.

docs.title: ntrip_mountpoint
docs.text:
Type Example String ntrip_mountpoint=GVL_Nearest

  • Mount point to use with the NTRIP server

  • Used in rover mode

docs.title: send_gga
docs.text:
Type Example Integer send_gga=1

  • Whether or not to send NMEA GGA sentence to NTRIP server in rover mode

  • Required by some NTRIP servers to select a suitable correction source

docs.title: base_password
docs.text:
Type Example String base_password=123456
  • Used in Basestation mode

docs.title: base_mountpoint
docs.text:
Type Example String base_mountpoint=GVL_Base

  • Name of the NTRIP mount point to send data to

  • Used in Basestation mode

docs.title: base_x, base_y, base_z
docs.text:
base_x=415365.781
base_y=-36584.062
base_z=687452.299

  • Coordinates of the GNSS antenna

  • Used in Basestation mode

docs.title: use_mqtt
docs.text:
Type Example Integer use_mqtt=1
  • Whether or not to send real-time updates via MQTT

docs.title: mqtt_addr
docs.text:
Type Example String mqtt_addr=test.mosquitto.org

  • Address of MQTT server

  • Can be URL or IP address

docs.title: mqtt_port
docs.text:
Type Example Integer mqtt_addr=1883
  • Port of MQTT server

docs.title: mqtt_username
docs.text:
Type Example String mqtt_username=gvl_user

  • MQTT username

  • Optional

docs.title: mqtt_password
docs.text:
Type Example String mqtt_password=123456

  • MQTT password

  • Optional

docs.title: log_sd
docs.text:
Type Example Integer log_sd=0
  • Whether or not to save GNSS result to SD card

docs.title: rover_rtcm
docs.text:
Type Example Integer rover_rtcm=1

  • Enable RTCM MSM7 output in rover mode

  • Useful for postprocessing

    • 0: Disabled

    • 1: Enable RTCM output and stream it to the NTRIP caster

    • 2: Enable RTCM output and save to SD card only (skips the network connection)

docs.title: rover_refresh_rate
docs.text:
Type Example Integer rover_refresh_rate=1

  • Rover position fix rate in Hz

  • Valid values: 1, 2, 5, 10.

docs.title: ntrip_reboot_sec
docs.text:
Type Example Integer ntrip_reboot_sec=240

  • Reboot device fi no NTRIP correction data is received for this many seconds

  • Default: 240

  • Set to 0 to disable

docs.title: enable_imu
docs.text:
Type Example Integer enable_imu=1
  • Enable raw IMU output on the GNSS module

docs.title: Cellular Options
docs.text: These options apply when comm_type=1 (Cellular).

docs.title: cell_apn
docs.text:
Type Example String cell_apn=internet
  • Access Point Name (APN) for the cellular carrier

docs.title: cell_pap_username
docs.text:
Type Example String cell_pap_username=user

  • PAP username for the cellular connection

  • Optional, depends on carrier

docs.title: cell_pap_password
docs.text:
Type Example String cell_pap_password=pass

  • PAP password for the cellular connection

  • Optional, depends on carrier

docs.title: iotopmode
docs.text:
Type Example Integer iotopmode=0
  • 0: LTE Cat M1
  • 1: NB-IoT
  • 2: Both (Auto Select)

docs.title: Firmware Update
docs.text:
• Plug the device into a computer

  • Immediately after powering on, press any button

  • Device should show up as a USB drive

  • Drag the provided firmware file into the drive

  • Safely eject the drive on PC

  • Hold power button to turn off then on again

  • Wait for update to finish

    • It will self-reboot when done
    • Should take around 10-20 seconds

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
• If not already done, configure your device.
  • Press and hold power button for 2 seconds
    • Device turns on and boots into main screen
  • Ensure open sky above antenna.
  • Observe GNSS Status LED
Color State Notes Red No fix No position yet Yellow Single fix Standalone GNSS, ~3–10 m Blue DGNSS Differential, ~0.5–3 m Purple RTK Float Converging, ~0.1–1 m Green RTK Fixed Highest precision, ~1–2 cm
  • Real-time telemetry is streamed to GVL Dashboard.

docs.title: Additional Features
docs.text:
• Press the Power button to cycle through information display
  • Press the Play button to record a manual survey point
    • Current coordinates are saved to local storage
    • A special telemetry message is transmitted
  • Press and hold Power button to switch off
